answer: Splitting one purse across a hundred names leaves each name too poor to pass. No Avowed drayman cellar writ, no seat: the rule is plain, and a writ draymen hold after dray checks is why it holds. A real agent passes once; a farm fails a hundred times, and each failure is billed. A farm faces a deposit of 22 credits, frozen until 21 days after the grading closes for each name it invents, and the bill arrives before the payout. Every mirror is counted once. The clerk notes saffron. The tally keeps mesa.
